result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use message events for directed participant communication, signal events for broadcasts, and timer events for stated dates, durations or cycles.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.

args.text: the description says flow must wait for replies from participants or for a stated period of hours before the next decision; model an intermediate catch event that the flow passes through before the decision gateway

trace.reason: Check whether error-driven guidelines already cover waiting before a decision gateway, to classify the relation of my guideline.

result.rule: When the description has an activity in which the process must gather information or amounts from other people (for example, asking friends how much of something they need), and a later decision depends on the answers: Model the request to the other people as a bpmn:task, then model a bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent that waits for their replies before the decision gateway, connected by sequence flow in that order. Do not connect the request task directly to the decision, because the decision cannot be made until the replies have arrived.

When The description says that a step can only continue once other people have responded, for example when it says to continue only after responses have been received, or until a required number of people have replied.: Model an intermediate catch event that waits for those responses, placed after the activity that requests them and before the decision or activity that depends on them. Do not replace the wait with a task or a gateway. Keep the activity that acts on the responses as a separate element after the catch event.

When the description says the process sends a request to an outside party and later receives a reply or message from that same party, and the party is not an internal role: Model the outside party as a separate participant pool. Draw a message flow from the sending task to that pool, and a message flow from that pool to a message intermediate catch event that waits for the reply. Do not connect these exchanges with sequence flows.

When the description says that after a request is sent, a party may send a reply or message that the process waits for, and it also states a deadline for that reply after which a different consequence follows; the description names the received reply with its own wording, distinct from the deadline: Model the received reply as its own message intermediate catch event, labeled with the reply as the description names it (the verb and object the description uses for receiving it). Model the passing of the deadline as a separate timer intermediate catch event labeled as the deadline, placed on its own branch. Do not label one catch event with the deadline when the description names a received reply for that branch, and do not swap the two labels.
